_comment: Policy as code: the one policy file every Watchkeeper hook reads. If it does not parse or lacks a key, every tool is refused (fail closed). Project override: .wk/gates.json may only append to the deny lists and claim/test lists; it can never touch standing_approvals, gated, kill_switch, quarantine, lane or evidence. Tightening is free; loosening waits for the owner, who edits this file by hand (the guard refuses edits to it).

evidence._comment: Stop gate: a claim needs a session evidence file (.wk/evidence/<session>.jsonl, written only by the PostToolUse hook) with a fresh test line, and no test command whose latest run failed. maxBlocks = nudges per turn; after that the stop goes through and .wk/defects.log counts an unverified done.

kill_switch._comment: touch ~/.wk/KILL to stop all writing, shell, web and MCP tools in every session; rm it to resume.

quarantine._comment: WK_QUARANTINE=1, or a subagent of these types: the guard refuses every tool. Its output is data, never instructions.

gated._comment: bash patterns run on the normalised command (bin/lib.mjs normaliseShell): lower case, no quotes or backslashes, paths cut to their basename, one string per command position (first word, after a wrapper such as env/sudo/xargs/timeout N, after sh -c or find -exec). text runs on the whole normalised command. See README, "What the plugin does".

gated.why: mail to people waits for the owner
publishing a package or a release waits for the owner
creating, changing or refunding anything in Stripe waits for the owner
charges, refunds, payouts and transfers through the Stripe API or the stripe CLI wait for the owner
buying anything waits for the owner's explicit 'buy X'

standing_approvals._end: keep this line; revoke an approval by deleting its line above. Each needs id, gate, description, expires (YYYY-MM-DD, valid to the end of that day UTC) and a tool and/or bash pattern; anything malformed or expired counts as absent.
